title: Kyoto-to-Shingu Overnight Sightseeing Train Returns
paragraphs: A special overnight sightseeing train in Japan has returned for the summer, taking passengers from Kyoto to the coast of the Kii Peninsula.

The train is called the WEST EXPRESS Ginga, and it is run by West Japan Railway Company, or JR West. In 2026, it ran from July 3 to September 30 between Kyoto and Shingu, a town on the coast of Wakayama Prefecture. There were 24 round trips. This is the sixth year that the train has run on this route.

The trip to Shingu is an overnight journey. The train leaves Kyoto at 9:13 p.m. and arrives in Shingu at 9:35 a.m. the next morning, so the trip takes more than 12 hours. On the way back, the train runs during the day. It leaves Shingu at 1:05 p.m. and arrives in Kyoto at 8:53 p.m.

The train is not just a way to travel. It also makes long stops at stations so that passengers can enjoy local food. For example, at Wakayama Station, passengers can buy Wakayama ramen to take away. At Kushimoto Station, the train stops for about an hour. There, passengers can eat a tuna cutlet burger or take a bus to see Hashigui-iwa, a famous line of rocks in the sea. In Shingu, overnight passengers can join a tour of Kumano Hayatama Taisha, an important shrine.

On board, guides talk about the area's nature, and there are also talks about rockets and space. During the day, there are quizzes and events in a shared space in the fourth car. Students from Wakayama University hand out maps and run quizzes for passengers.
All seats must be reserved. A normal seat that leans back costs 8,670 yen, and a private room costs 15,380 yen. According to JR West, tickets for the first trip of the season sold out quickly.
From October, the train will run on a different route, between Kyoto and Shimonoseki.
